title: Needlepoint kneeler cushion
subtitle: A firm 25 by 30 cm kneeler top in basketweave tent stitch on 13-count canvas with a geometric cross motif
excerpt: A kneeler is worked to the same pattern as a large pincushion: a firm tent stitch canvas top, canvas or velvet sides, and a dense inner pad. This design centres a simple geometric cross on a two-colour field in basketweave tent stitch. Finished top size is 25 by 30 cm.
sourceNotes: Kneeler construction from Weldon's Practical Needlework, church canvaswork series (1890s). Geometric cross motif synthesised from Victorian canvaswork geometric examples in Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882).

glossaryTerms.definition: The dense inner foam or stuffed pad that gives a kneeler its firm, load-bearing structure. A kneeler pad needs to be firmer than a cushion pad: high-density foam or tightly packed wool batting.

heroPrompt: A needlepoint kneeler on a church pew showing a geometric cross motif in dark red and cream, basketweave stitch texture visible, natural stone church light.

content.text: A kneeler top is worked as a tent stitch panel and then assembled over a firm pad. The construction requires the canvas to be durable, the thread coverage complete, and the pad inside dense enough to take repeated use. This design is a 130 by 156 hole rectangle on 13-count canvas, finishing at 25 by 30 cm. The central motif is a bold geometric cross in a contrast colour on a dark background.
What you need

items.label: Canvas
items.value: 13-count double-thread (Penelope) canvas or mono canvas, cut 36 by 41 cm (leaves a 5 cm margin). Double-thread canvas is more durable for a floor piece

items.label: Thread: main (background)
items.value: Tapestry wool, 2 strands. Suggested: DMC Laine à broder 930 / Anchor Tapisserie 8636 (dark antique blue). About 80 m

items.label: Thread: cross motif
items.value: Tapestry wool, 2 strands. Suggested: DMC Laine à broder 712 / Anchor Tapisserie 9386 (cream). About 30 m

items.label: Thread: cross accent
items.value: Tapestry wool, 2 strands. Suggested: DMC Laine à broder 816 / Anchor Tapisserie 9646 (garnet). About 15 m

items.label: Needle
items.value: Tapestry size 18 (for double canvas and tapestry wool)

items.label: Frame
items.value: Scroll frame, 30 by 35 cm working area

items.label: Kneeler pad
items.value: High-density foam block cut to 25 by 30 by 8 cm, or an existing kneeler pad to fit

items.label: Side fabric
items.value: Heavy canvas or upholstery velvet for the kneeler sides, about 75 by 10 cm

items.label: Strong thread
items.value: Linen or upholstery thread for assembly

content.text: Palette
Background: DMC Laine à broder 930 / Anchor Tapisserie 8636: dark antique blue
Cross: DMC Laine à broder 712 / Anchor Tapisserie 9386: cream
Accent: DMC Laine à broder 816 / Anchor Tapisserie 9646: garnet
Stretching the canvas
Mount on a scroll frame and keep the canvas under tension throughout. A kneeler that is worked slack will be uneven when the pad is inserted.
Stitches used
Basketweave tent stitch
throughout. Use two strands of tapestry wool on 13-count canvas for better coverage and durability at floor level.
Working method
Mark the design boundary and the cross motif position. The cross is 30 holes wide and 60 holes tall, centred on the 130 by 156 hole panel, with a 4-hole wide crossbar at mid-height.
Work the cross motif in cream. Add the garnet accent as a narrow two-hole border around the cross arms.
Fill the dark background in basketweave. Ensure every hole is covered; bare canvas threads on a floor-use piece will abrade quickly.
Block by dampening and pinning square overnight.
Finishing
Trim the canvas margin to 2 cm. Assemble the kneeler by placing the
kneeler pad

face down on the reverse of the worked canvas. Fold the canvas margins firmly up over the pad edges. Overcast the corner seams. Sew the side fabric around the pad, joining it to the canvas margin at the top and tucking it under at the base. Slip-stitch a piece of felt or heavy canvas to the base.
What to try next

A matching pair of kneelers with two complementary geometric motifs on a shared background colour suits a pew end. Working both pieces on the same large canvas sheet before cutting ensures the background colour matches exactly.
